title: Purity bias masquerades as an adiposity signal in purified human adipocytes, while adipose-tissue UFM1 tracks eIF2α/PERK-dependent ER stress and the UFMylation imbalance index normalises after bariatric surgery: a multi-cohort transcriptomic study

description:
Reproducible analysis code and per-figure/per-table source data for a pure re-analysis (no new samples) of publicly available human adipose-tissue transcriptomic datasets.

The study's central methodological finding is that an apparent UFM1–adiposity association observed in purified mature adipocytes is a cell-composition (purity) artefact: once a non-adipocyte contamination axis and a technical/housekeeping axis are partialled out, the association collapses. In bulk adipose tissue, by contrast, UFM1 reproducibly tracks eIF2α/PERK-dependent endoplasmic-reticulum stress across independent cohorts, and a composite UFMylation imbalance index normalises after bariatric surgery.

Data provenance (all third-party and public): GEO accessions GSE70353 (discovery, n=770), GSE176171 (single-nucleus atlas), GSE174475 (purified adipocytes), GSE245948 (independent RNA-seq), GSE59034, GSE72158 and GSE53376 (paired bariatric-surgery cohorts); and eQTL Catalogue QTD000116 (GTEx V8 subcutaneous adipose) for the UFM1 cis-eQTL query. Raw inputs are not bundled; see the repository README for file names and reproduction steps.

Software: Python (pandas, numpy, scipy, statsmodels, scikit-learn, matplotlib, gseapy); pinned versions in code/requirements.txt. Ensembl identifiers were verified against Ensembl xrefs/symbol and mygene (species = Homo sapiens).

This deposit accompanies a manuscript submitted to PeerJ.
notes: Analysis code and source data only. The underlying biological datasets remain the property of their original GEO / eQTL Catalogue deposits.
